'''Guido De Philippis''' (born [[August 16]], [[1985]] at [[Fiesole]]) is an [[Italians|Italian]] [[mathematician]]. He works on [[Calculus of variations|the calculus of variations]], [[partial differential equation]]s and [[geometric measure theory]].

In 2016, he was awarded the [[EMS Prize]], "for his outstanding contributions to the regularity of solutions of [[Monge–Ampère equation]] and [[optimal map]]s and for his deep work on quantitative stability inequalities for the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian and rigidity in some [[isoperimetric inequality|isoperimetric type inequalities]].".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/system/files/news/Druck%20-%20pp_3657_Broschuere%20-%207ECM.pdf |title=7ECM : Berlin 2016 Laureates |website=Euro-math-soc.eu |access-date=2016-08-29 |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006190620/http://euro-math-soc.eu/system/files/news/Druck%20-%20pp_3657_Broschuere%20-%207ECM.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2018 he was awarded the [[Stampacchia Medal]]. In 2021, he received the ISAAC award.

De Philippis was a PhD student of [[Luigi Ambrosio]] and [[Luis Caffarelli]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=171713 |title=Guido De Philippis – The Mathematics Genealogy Project |website=Genealogy.ams.org |date= |access-date=2016-08-29}}</ref>
